title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: §50 'Enveloppes schématiques de groupes discrets' (cas unibranche). G is a group scheme locally of finite presentation over S; the important case is S = Spec Z. A section g ∈ G(S) is called unipotent if, on every geometric fibre, g_s̄ = φ_s̄(1) for some homomorphism φ_s̄ : G_a → G_k̄. The previous page states the easy direction: if a global homomorphism φ : G_{a,S} → G with φ(1) = g exists, then g is unipotent.

This page begins with (4) φ(1) = g and asks whether the converse holds 'dans le bon cas'. In other words: does fibrewise unipotence of g imply that a homomorphism G_{a,S} → G with φ(1) = g exists over the whole base?

Case S = Spec K, char K = 0. φ is unique: φ(t) = exp(t log g), equivalently g^t. By fpqc descent, a φ' found after a faithfully flat quasi-compact extension S' → S is invariant under the descent data and so descends. Hence over a field of characteristic 0 the answer is yes.

Case char p > 0. Uniqueness fails because End(G_a) is large. There are additive polynomials f with f(1) = 1, for example Frobenius x ↦ x^p, or x ↦ x + c(x^p − x). Composing φ with such an f gives another φ with the same value at 1; equivalently, x^p − x is a nontrivial endomorphism vanishing at 1. So descent from k̄ to k cannot be run naively.

Grothendieck suggests rescuing the argument by some canonical choice: e.g. a uniqueness statement for a distinguished class of φ, or a unique subgroup of G (image of φ) attached to g. He asks whether this holds at least over a field. He declares these questions open and 'assez intéressantes'.

The next page carries the global strategy:
- spread out from the characteristic-0 generic point to a nonempty open U;
- use uniqueness to get a largest such U;
- localize at a maximal point of S∖U;
- reduce to S a trait (S regular of dimension 1), where one must extend φ_U across the closed point.

Purpose: to have a good notion of unipotent and quasi-unipotent sections (images of inertia / Dehn-twist-type generators) in schematic envelopes over Z of discrete groups such as fundamental groups, for the Galois–Teichmüller programme.
errors: The definition of 'unipotent' on the previous page (g_s̄ = φ(1) for some φ: G_a → G) is not the standard notion in characteristic p. The image of G_a has exponent p, so a Jordan block of size > p in GL_n (order p^2) is unipotent in the usual sense but not in Grothendieck's sense. In char p his notion means 'lies on a one-parameter additive subgroup', which forces g^p = 1.

The hoped-for necessity (fibrewise unipotent ⇒ exists φ: G_{a,S} → G with φ(1) = g) fails even for G = GL_5 over the trait Z_(2). Take g = 1 + N with N the superdiagonal matrix with entries (1, 2, 1, 2). Mod 2, N̄ = E12 + E34 and N̄² = 0, so g mod 2 = φ̄(1) with φ̄(t) = 1 + tN̄. On the generic fibre g is unipotent with unique φ(t) = Σ_k binom(t,k) N^k. Since N^4 = 4E15, the t^4-coefficient of φ is (4/24)E15 = (1/6)E15, which is not in Z_(2). By uniqueness on the generic fibre and flatness, no φ exists over Z_(2). So the extension step over a trait that he plans on the next page cannot succeed in general. Some 'bon cas' hypothesis is needed, e.g. residue characteristic p ≥ n for a faithful n-dimensional representation (when N^p = 0, the coefficients N^k/k! for k < p are integral). This is the regime of Serre's saturation.

ideas.what: In char 0 a unipotent element lies on a unique one-parameter additive subgroup, φ(t) = exp(t log g); uniqueness yields fpqc descent of φ.
ideas.modern_name: Exponential/logarithm for unipotent elements; uniqueness of the G_a through a unipotent element in characteristic 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lie theory; Borel, Chevalley); descent is standard SGA1/SGA3
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA3 style arguments; not specifically located

ideas.what: Non-uniqueness in char p caused by endomorphisms of G_a fixing 1 (Frobenius, x ↦ x + c(x^p − x)); question whether a canonical φ or a canonical subgroup containing g exists, at least over a field.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical one-parameter subgroups / saturation of unipotent elements of order p; 'good' A1-overgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (saturation, 1990s); Testerman (1995); Seitz (2000); McNinch ('optimal SL2', 2000s); Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran (2017)

ideas.what: Integral question: is a fibrewise unipotent section of a group scheme over Z (or over a trait) the value at 1 of a homomorphism G_{a,S} → G? Strategy via spreading out from char 0 and extension across codimension-1 points.
ideas.modern_name: Integral exponentials / extension of one-parameter subgroups over mixed-characteristic bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partly Serre and Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran (exponentials when p is large relative to the representation); no single standard reference

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses the question whether fibrewise unipotence of a section of a group scheme over Z implies a global homomorphism G_a → G through it, and whether in char p there is a canonical choice of φ or a canonical subgroup. He states he has no answer. The global version fails in general (GL_5 over Z_(2) counterexample above). The field version in char p is essentially what Serre's saturation and Seitz/McNinch's 'good/optimal' one-parameter subgroups later answered, under 'good characteristic' / p ≥ n hypotheses.
missed.quote: Je n'ai pas encore de réponse à ces questions (assez intéressantes !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck, in the context of schematic envelopes of discrete groups (Galois–Teichmüller), anticipating the problem of canonical exponentiation of unipotent elements in characteristic p. That problem became Serre's saturation theory and the Seitz/McNinch work. It also identifies an integral version over Spec Z / traits that seems less studied and matters for integral models of unipotent or Malcev envelopes of fundamental groups.

missed.claim: Links quasi-unipotent sections of schematic envelopes over Z of discrete groups (the monodromy-theorem phenomenon) with the char-p uniqueness problem for one-parameter subgroups. This bridge between anabelian/Teichmüller envelopes and Serre-type saturation does not appear to be made explicitly in the literature.
missed.quote: En car. p>0 la difficulté provient du fait qu'il y a des homomorphismes de groupes G_a → G_a (tels x ↦ x^p − x) qui ne sont pas triviaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral (Spec Z) completions of fundamental groups and their unipotent elements (images of Dehn twists, inertia) appear in current work on integral/p-adic unipotent fundamental groups. The precise conditions under which inertia generators lie on integral G_a's are relevant there.

deep.surprise_reason: A genuinely open-at-the-time question that anticipates Serre's saturation and the Seitz/McNinch canonical-subgroup work. However, the page contains only the question and the standard char-0 descent argument, no result. The integral form he hopes for is in fact false without hypotheses on p relative to G.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads 'tel que soit' followed by '(4) φ(1) = g': it continues the condition from the previous page, 'Pour que g soit unipotente, il faut et il suffit qu'il existe un homom. φ: G_a → G tel que...'.
'qui permet d'affirmer[?]' is likely 'qui permet d'appliquer la théorie de descente'.
The descent clause reads roughly 'si après extension S' → S fidèlement plate quasi-compacte, il existe φ' ayant les propriétés voulues, alors φ existe (sur S lui-même)'.

The example endomorphism is x ↦ x^p − x (Artin–Schreier type), which vanishes at 1; 'triviaux sur 1' means 'nuls en 1'. The interlinear insertion is uncertain (possibly 'fondamentalement', not 'radiciels').

The end of the page is mostly illegible in the transcription. It appears to ask whether G has a unique (sous-)groupe ... contenant une section ..., 'pas trop triviale?', then 'Est-ce du moins vrai sur un corps de base ?'.
